description:
Problem: constructing the MCP server changes process-wide state. It sets the benchbox logger level (benchbox/mcp/server.py:93), turns on quiet mode, and its telemetry can install a global tracer provider (benchbox/mcp/telemetry.py:124). In-process callers such as scripts/doc_contracts.py:452 and :478 inherit the changes. On 2026-10-24 this contaminated later tests and contributed to the red trunk. #3385 contained it in the exporter only (tests/unit/scripts/test_doc_contracts.py:150). Saving and restoring globals is not a concurrency boundary.

Outcome: process-wide configuration moves to explicit startup at the existing run_server() boundary, with a migration for in-process callers. Stdio quietness and remote-log redaction are preserved.

Decision gates:
1. Public API. List every caller and the documented MCP API contract before editing. Existing tests expect construction to turn on quiet mode (tests/unit/mcp/test_mcp_stdout_isolation.py:15-28 and 101-120); changing that is a behaviour change and needs a changelog migration note. If an external consumer relies on construction side effects, stop and ask the owner.
2. Telemetry. A host application's tracer provider must not be replaced silently. Decide whether telemetry start becomes explicit or is skipped when a provider already exists, and record the choice.

Item guardrails: stdio startup stays quiet; remote rejection logs stay redacted; telemetry exports only intended spans; MCP tool contracts are unchanged.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no raw gh pr merge.
